source_data.subject: Class 10 Social Science (Geography - Contemporary India II)

details: Everything in the environment that is technologically accessible, economically feasible, and culturally acceptable to satisfy human needs.
Human beings interact with nature through technology and create institutions to accelerate economic development.
evidence_or_examples: Transformation of crude mineral oil into refined petrochemicals through modern refining infrastructure.

details: By Origin: Biotic (living organisms, flora, fauna) and Abiotic (non-living items, rocks, metals).
By Exhaustibility: Renewable (solar, wind, water) and Non-Renewable (fossil fuels, minerals).
By Ownership: Individual (plots, houses), Community (pastures, burial grounds), National (roads, railways, within 12 nautical miles), International (oceanic beyond 200 nautical miles EEZ).
By Status of Development: Potential (found but unutilized), Developed (surveyed and quantified), Stock (lack technological access), Reserves (subset of stock stored for future).
evidence_or_examples: Solar and wind power potential in Rajasthan and Gujarat; Hydrogen water splitting as Stock.

details: Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations or damaging the environment.
Adopted at the 1992 Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit to achieve global sustainable development and combat poverty and disease.
evidence_or_examples: First International Earth Summit (1992) attended by over 100 heads of state in Brazil.

details: 1. Identification and inventory through surveying, mapping, and qualitative/quantitative estimation.
2. Evolving a planning structure endowed with appropriate technology, skill, and institutional set-up.
3. Matching resource development plans with overall national development plans.
evidence_or_examples: Arunachal Pradesh has abundant water but lacks infrastructure; Ladakh is culturally rich but isolated from water and minerals.

details: 3.28 million sq km total geographical area of India; land use data available for 93%.
Categories: Forests, Land not available for cultivation (Barren/Waste, Non-agricultural use), Fallow lands (Current fallow, Other fallow), Net Sown Area, Gross Cropped Area.
evidence_or_examples: Net Sown Area is over 80% in Punjab and Haryana, but under 10% in Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.

sub_branches.concept: Causes of Land Degradation & Conservation Measures
details: Degradation Drivers: Over-irrigation (Punjab, Haryana), Mining & Overburden waste (Jharkhand, Odisha, MP), Overgrazing (Gujarat, Rajasthan).
Conservation Techniques: Afforestation, Contour Ploughing, Terrace Farming, Strip Cropping, Shelter Belts.
evidence_or_examples: Salinization of soil due to tube-well over-irrigation in northwestern plains.

sub_branches.concept: Six Major Soil Types in India
details: Alluvial Soil: Most widespread, deposited by Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra; classified into Khadar (new, fertile) and Bangar (old, nodular).
Black/Regur Soil: Deccan trap region, basaltic, rich in calcium carbonate and potash, ideal for cotton.
Red and Yellow Soil: Develops on crystalline igneous rocks in low rainfall areas; reddish due to iron diffusion.
Laterite Soil: Heavy leaching due to tropical rains, acidic, humus poor; good for cashew nuts with manures.
Arid Soil: Sandy texture, saline, high salt content, lacks moisture and humus.
Forest Soil: Loamy and silty in valley sides, coarse-grained in upper slopes; acidic with low humus.
evidence_or_examples: Cotton cultivation in Maharashtra Regur soils; Cashew plantations in Tamil Nadu and Kerala laterite soils.

sub_branches.concept: Rich Flora and Fauna & Threat Dynamics
details: India holds nearly 8% of total global species richness (approx 1.6 million species).
Over 10% of recorded wild flora and 20% of mammals are on the threatened list.
evidence_or_examples: Cheetah (declared extinct in India in 1952), Pink-headed Duck, Mountain Quail, Forest Owlet.

details: Normal Species: Population levels considered normal for survival (Cattle, Sal, Pine).
Endangered Species: In danger of extinction if adverse factors continue (Blackbuck, Crocodile, Lion-tailed Macaque).
Vulnerable Species: Population declined to levels likely to move into endangered (Blue Sheep, Asiatic Elephant, Gangetic Dolphin).
Rare Species: Small population that may move into endangered/vulnerable (Himalayan Brown Bear, Wild Asiatic Buffalo).
Endemic Species: Found only in specific isolated geographical areas (Andaman Teal, Nicobar Pigeon).
Extinct Species: Not found after searches in known areas (Asiatic Cheetah).
evidence_or_examples: Asiatic Cheetah declared extinct in 1952; Gangetic Dolphin categorized as Vulnerable.

details: 1972 Act: Enacted an all-India list of protected species, banned hunting, and restricted wildlife trade.
Project Tiger (1973): Premier conservation initiative saving flagship mammal species across national tiger reserves.
evidence_or_examples: Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand), Sundarbans (West Bengal), Sariska (Rajasthan), Periyar (Kerala).

details: Reserved Forests: More than 50% of total forest land; permanently earmarked for conservation under strict state control.
Protected Forests: Almost 1/3rd of total forest area; protected from further depletion.
Unclassed Forests: Other forests and wastelands belonging to government and private individuals/communities.
evidence_or_examples: Jammu & Kashmir and MP have high Reserved forests; North-Eastern states have high Unclassed forests.

details: Chipko Movement: Resisted Himalayan deforestation by physically hugging trees.
Beej Bachao Andolan & Navdanya: Restored traditional organic crops without chemical inputs in Tehri.
Joint Forest Management (JFM): Formally passed in Odisha (1988), engaging village communities to restore degraded state forests.
Sacred Groves: Pristine forest patches protected through traditional nature worship.
evidence_or_examples: Munda and Santhal tribes worshipping Mahua and Kadamba trees; Sariska villagers citing Wildlife Act against mining.

details: Water covers 71% of Earth's surface, but fresh water constitutes only 2.5%.
Quantitative Scarcity: Driven by over-exploitation, growing population, and regional rainfall variation.
Qualitative Scarcity: Abundant water rendered unfit for human use due to domestic sewage, industrial effluents, pesticides, and chemical fertilizers.
evidence_or_examples: Arid Rajasthan facing physical shortage; urban rivers suffering from toxic chemical pollution.

details: Proclaimed by Nehru as 'Temples of Modern India' integrating agriculture with rapid industrialization.
Key Benefits: Hydroelectricity, irrigation canal networks, flood control, inland navigation, fish breeding.
Drawbacks & Opposition: Excessive reservoir sedimentation, river fragmentation, loss of aquatic life, land submergence, involuntary human displacement.
evidence_or_examples: Bhakra-Nangal (Sutlej-Beas), Hirakud (Mahanadi), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada), Narmada Bachao Andolan.

details: Guls/Kuls: Diversion channels in Western Himalayas for agriculture.
Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting: Direct harvesting of clean rainfall into underground Tankas in arid Rajasthan (Phalodi, Bikaner).
Khadins and Johads: Rain-fed storage structures in agricultural fields.
Bamboo Drip Irrigation: 200-year-old system in Meghalaya tapping hill stream water using gravity bamboo pipes.
Mandatory Rainwater Harvesting: Tamil Nadu became the first state making rooftop systems legally compulsory.
evidence_or_examples: Gendathur village in Mysuru installing rooftop harvesting in 200 households; Bamboo piping in Meghalaya.

details: Primitive Subsistence: Small patches, family labor, simple tools (hoe, dao), slash-and-burn (Jhumming).
Intensive Subsistence: High population pressure on land, high chemical inputs and irrigation to maximize yield.
Commercial Farming: Large land holdings, high HYV seeds, synthetic fertilizers, mechanization for market export.
evidence_or_examples: Jhumming in North-Eastern states; Rice cultivation in Punjab as commercial crop vs Odisha as subsistence.

details: Kharif: Sown June-July (monsoon onset), harvested Sept-Oct (Paddy, Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Cotton, Jute).
Rabi: Sown Oct-Dec (winter onset), harvested April-June (Wheat, Barley, Gram, Mustard).
Zaid: Short summer season between March-June (Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, Fodder crops).
evidence_or_examples: Paddy in monsoon belts; Wheat production in western Himalayan winter precipitation belts.

branches.theme: Major Food, Cash, and Non-Food Crops

details: Rice: Staple food, hot & humid climate (>25°C), high rainfall (>100 cm), clayey alluvial soil (WB, UP, Punjab).
Wheat: Cool growing season (10-15°C), bright sunshine ripening (21-26°C), 50-75 cm rainfall (Punjab, Haryana, UP).
Millets: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi (rich in iron/calcium, drought resilient).
Sugarcane: Tropical/subtropical crop, 21-27°C, 75-100 cm rainfall (UP, Maharashtra).
Tea & Coffee: Plantation beverage crops; Tea in Assam/WB; Coffee (Arabica variety) in Baba Budan Hills, Karnataka.
Rubber & Fiber Crops: Rubber in Kerala (>200 cm rain); Cotton (black Regur soil, 210 frost-free days); Jute (golden fiber, Hugli basin).
evidence_or_examples: Kerala leading in natural rubber; Maharashtra leading in cotton; West Bengal leading in jute.

details: Land Reforms: Land consolidation (Chakbandi), abolition of Zamindari system.
Green Revolution & White Revolution (Operation Flood): Modern HYV technological inputs.
Institutional Protection: Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Personal Accident Insurance Scheme (PAIS), Minimum Support Price (MSP).
Bhoodan-Gramdan Movement: Initiated by Vinoba Bhave ('Bloodless Revolution') for voluntary land redistribution.
evidence_or_examples: Shri Ram Chandra Reddy offering 80 acres in Pochampally; MSP announcements protecting farmers from market drops.

details: 1. Veins and Lodes: Cracks and fissures in Igneous/Metamorphic rocks (Tin, Copper, Zinc, Lead).
2. Beds and Layers: Accumulation in Sedimentary rock strata (Coal, Iron Ore, Gypsum).
3. Residual Mass: Weathering of surface rocks leaving residual material (Bauxite).
4. Placer Deposits: Alluvial deposits in valley floor sands, non-corrosive (Gold, Silver, Platinum).
5. Ocean Waters & Beds: Soluble salts and seabed deposits (Common salt, Magnesium, Manganese nodules).
evidence_or_examples: Khetri copper mines in Rajasthan (lodes); Monazite sands in Kerala (placer).

details: Iron Ore: Magnetite (70% iron, high magnetic quality), Hematite (50-60% iron, major industrial ore). Major belts: Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru, Maharashtra-Goa.
Manganese: Essential for steel manufacturing (10 kg manganese per ton of steel); Odisha top producer.
Bauxite: Aluminum ore; lightweight, high conductivity, malleable; Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput, Odisha.
Copper: Malleable, ductile, good conductor; Balaghat mines (MP), Khetri (Rajasthan), Singhbhum (Jharkhand).
Mica: Excellent di-electric strength, low power loss factor, insulating; Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt (Jharkhand).
evidence_or_examples: Kudremukh iron ore slurry pipeline to Mangaluru port; Balaghat copper mines producing 52% of India's copper.

details: Coal: Gondwana coal (200 million years old, metallurgical coking coal) and Tertiary coal (55 million years old, NE states). Varieties: Anthracite, Bituminous, Lignite, Peat.
Petroleum: Trapped in anticlines and fault traps; Mumbai High, Ankleshwar (Gujarat), Digboi (Assam - oldest oilfield).
Natural Gas: Environmentally friendly fuel; HVJ (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur) cross-country pipeline.
Non-Conventional: Solar (Rajasthan/Gujarat), Wind (Nagarcoil to Madurai in TN), Biogas (Gobar gas plants), Tidal (Gulf of Khambhat), Geothermal (Manikaran in HP, Puga Valley in Ladakh).
evidence_or_examples: Digboi as India's oldest operating oilfield; HVJ pipeline transporting gas over 1,700 km.

details: Backbone of development: Modernizes agriculture, reduces heavy dependence on agricultural income, reduces poverty and unemployment.
Agglomeration Economies: Cost advantages gained when industries cluster near urban centers to utilize banking, transport, power, and market networks.
evidence_or_examples: Cotton textile cluster around Mumbai and Ahmedabad urban centers.

details: Textile Industry: Self-reliant and complete in value chain (fiber to garment); Cotton (Mumbai 1854), Jute (Hugli basin cluster in WB).
Sugar Industry: Seasonal nature; shifting from UP to Maharashtra due to higher sucrose content and successful cooperatives.
Iron & Steel Industry: Basic/Heavy industry; raw material ratio Iron ore : Coking coal : Limestone = 4 : 2 : 1. Concentrated in Chhota Nagpur Plateau.
Aluminum Smelting: Second major metallurgical industry; requires massive continuous electricity and cheap bauxite.
Chemicals & Fertilizers: Organic and inorganic chemicals; Nitrogenous (Urea), Phosphatic, and NPK fertilizers.
Information Technology & Electronics: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI); Bengaluru as Silicon Valley of India.
evidence_or_examples: STPI hubs generating 30% employment for women; Chhota Nagpur plateau holding majority steel plants.

details: Four Pollution Types: Air (toxic gases, smoke stacks), Water (industrial effluents), Thermal (hot water discharge into rivers), Noise (generators, machinery).
Effluent Treatment Stages: Primary (mechanical screening/sedimentation), Secondary (biological aeration), Tertiary (chemical recycling to zero discharge).
NTPC EMS ISO 14001: Model corporate strategy for ash utilization, ecological monitoring, and green belts around thermal power plants.
evidence_or_examples: NTPC power plants achieving high fly ash utilization and establishing environmental monitoring cells.

details: India has one of the largest road networks globally (approx 5.6 million km).
Road Network Classification: Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways (Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai), National Highways (NHAI), State Highways (PWD), District Roads, Border Roads (BRO).
Advantages: Lower construction capital, flexible terrain handling, door-to-door delivery, feeder network to rail and ports.
evidence_or_examples: North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) and East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar).

details: Railways: Primary mode for heavy long-distance freight and passenger transit; network affected by terrain (dense in Northern Plains, sparse in Himalayas).
Pipelines: Modern transport for crude oil, petroleum, and natural gas; zero transit delays/losses (e.g., HVJ pipeline).
Inland Waterways: National Waterways (NW-1 Ganga between Allahabad and Haldia, NW-2 Brahmaputra between Sadiya and Dhubri).

Major Seaports: 12 Major and 200 notified non-major ports. Western Coast (Kandla/Deendayal, Mumbai, Marmagao, Mangaluru, Kochi); Eastern Coast (Tuticorin, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Haldia, Kolkata).
evidence_or_examples: Deendayal/Kandla tidal port developed post-1947 to relieve Mumbai port; Marmagao handling 50% iron ore exports.

sub_branches.concept: Mass Media, Digital Networks & Trade Balance
details: Personal & Mass Communication: Indian Postal Network (First Class mail: cards/envelopes; Second Class mail: book packets/newspapers), Telecom & Digital India, Doordarshan, Akashvani.
International Trade & Balance of Trade: Export vs Import monetary value. Favorable trade balance when exports > imports; Unfavorable when imports > exports.
Tourism as Invisible Trade: Earmarks massive foreign exchange, supports 15 million direct jobs, promotes national integration and cultural heritage.
evidence_or_examples: Foreign tourist arrivals spending foreign exchange directly on Indian hospitality, handicrafts, and heritage.
